by: gazette session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-1)
title: The New Zealand Gazette notices the old estate holds as text, as exported once from its tables

landmarks: one JSON object per line with keys notice, article, url, title, published_on, posted_on, old_type, old_article, text
notice numbers of the form <year>-<section code><n>

signals_note: Not a document the Gazette published: an export of the article text the old estate captured for each notice (incoming_news.articles at gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/ addresses) with its classifier's row (nzbn_canonical.gazette.notices), made once on 20 October 2026. Every row from it is 'taken from the old estate's tables; original not held'.
notes: 208,461 lines, 207,133 notice numbers: 1,328 notices were captured twice with slightly different text (none identical); the copy the old classifier read is kept. The notice number carries the Gazette's own section code and the notice's place in one sequence per year, so the family is exact. The text is flattened: block boundaries are glued ('LiquidatorsDennis'). Bankruptcy, prohibition and independent-celebrant notices print home addresses: the text is never published.
applies_to: every notice the old estate captured from gazette.govt.nz, 2000 to 16 October 2026
process: Type by the section code in the notice number; recognise a format by the notice's own words; a notice no reader recognises is held typed as 'not read'.
gates: Every export line is a notice or a second capture set aside.
The held numbers are checked against the Gazette's own numbering (check.py).

by: gazette session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-1); taken from the old estate's C226 profile and extended
title: A Registrar-General's list of marriage or civil-union celebrants (Gazette notice)

landmarks: 'celebrant' in the title, or in the first 3,000 characters with a section of the Marriage Act 1955 or the Civil Union Act 2004, or the printed header 'Name of Celebrant Name of Organisation'

signals_note: Recognised by the subject word, never by record shape alone: a bankruptcy list has a celebrant list's shape (the old estate measured 23,139 false positives of 24,875 on shape alone).
notes: Five list shapes: stops ('Surname, Given, Organisation.' and 'Surname, Given.' run together), address (the third field an address: independent celebrants under Marriage Act s 10 and 11 and the Civil Union Act; the address is private), chain ('Surname, Given Surname, Given' with no stops, most lists from 2019: the next surname is the chunk's last word with its particles, or the glue where the space was lost, checked against the list's alphabetical order), marked (the combined annual list from 2016: each name preceded by its letters M and/or CU under the printed key 'CU = Civil Union Celebrant M = Independent Marriage Celebrant'; the letters cut each chunk exactly and are kept as marks; a marked list that prints addresses, 2015, is set aside), table (no delimiter between the given names and the organisation: set aside), none (a notice with no list). The action is the notice's own words: appointment, removal, publication ('published for general information' is not an appointment), annual list (says both appointed and published: everyone holding the office for the period), or none when a removal stands beside anything else, or nothing.
applies_to: about 3,000 notices in section go, 2000 to 2026
process: Find the list after the operative sentence and before 'Dated'.
Decide the shape; split records; an address is kept private.
A notice whose action is none gives no rows, only a catch-log line.
gates: Every recognised notice gives records or a catch-log line.
Every record the reader cannot cut is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the record or the notice; publish the rest
